summary: This Wikipedia-derived note traces the origins and history of the German people, from the medieval emergence of a German ethnicity within East Francia and the Holy Roman Empire, through the Germanic tribes, Roman contact, and the Huns, to the 19th-century unification and post-World War II expulsions. It also covers the German language, German philosophy, the Reformation and Thirty Years' War, Jewish German history, and religious demographics in modern Germany.
one_line: Overview of the origins, language, philosophy, religion and history of the German people from the Middle Ages to the modern era.
key_facts: German ethnicity emerged in the Middle Ages from the formation of the kingdom of Germany within East Francia and later the Holy Roman Empire, beginning in the 9th century.
The title rex teutonicum, 'King of the Germans', was first used in the late 11th century by the chancery of Pope Gregory VII to describe Henry IV.
The five Germanic tribes considered major contributors to the formation of the Germans were the Saxons, Franci, Thuringii, Alamanni and Bavarii, sometimes with the Frisians included.
Roman emperor Augustus ordered the conquest of the Germans in 12 BC, but the Roman defeat at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest led Rome to abandon plans to completely conquer Germany.
German is a West Germanic language spoken by approximately 100 million native speakers and is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union.
The University of Berlin, founded in 1810 by linguist and philosopher Wilhelm von Humboldt, served as an influential model for a number of modern western universities.
In 1517, Martin Luther challenged the Catholic Church, which he saw as a corruption of Christian faith, and established Protestantism.

The Thirty Years' War (1618–1648) was one of the most destructive conflicts in European history and was fought largely as a religious conflict between Protestants and Catholics in the Holy Roman Empire.
In 1866 the Prussians defeated the Austrians at the Battle of Königgrätz, succeeding in creating the North German Confederation.
In the Franco-Prussian War, Prussia and its southern German allies, including Bavaria, were victorious over France in 1870, and the German Empire was created in 1871 as a German nation-state.
Yiddish developed as a mixed language incorporating major parts of the German language and elements of other European languages among Jews who assimilated into German culture.
Between 12 and 16.5 million ethnic Germans and German citizens were expelled westwards to allied-occupied Germany after World War II.
Kant played a central role in the history of philosophy, and Kantianism inspired the work of Schopenhauer and Nietzsche as well as German idealism defended by Fichte and Hegel.
According to the latest nationwide census, Roman Catholics constituted 30.8% of Germany's population and Evangelical Protestants 30.3%.

entities.name: Charlemagne
entities.role: Frankish king under whose rule the large tribes of modern Germany had been united by the 9th century, known in German as Karl der Große

entities.name: Henry IV
entities.role: future Holy Roman Emperor of the German Nation described as rex teutonicum by the chancery of Pope Gregory VII

entities.name: Pope Gregory VII
entities.role: pope whose chancery first used the title rex teutonicum in the late 11th century

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.role: Roman leader whose conflict with Germanic tribes forced major tribes to retreat to the east bank of the Rhine

entities.name: Augustus
entities.role: Roman emperor who in 12 BC ordered the conquest of the Germans

entities.name: Attila
entities.role: Hun leader whose Hunnic Empire included large numbers of Germans, and whose army was largely German; the empire collapsed after his unexpected death

entities.name: Martin Luther
entities.role: figure who challenged the Catholic Church in 1517 and established Protestantism

entities.name: Johann Tillmann of East Prussia
entities.role: young reformer and new German nationalist who sought to unite all German-speaking and ethnic-German people

entities.name: Wilhelm von Humboldt
entities.role: linguist and philosopher who founded the University of Berlin in 1810

entities.name: Kant
entities.role: philosopher who played a central role in the history of philosophy

entities.name: Leibniz

entities.name: Albertus Magnus
entities.role: medieval German philosopher who helped shape western philosophy

entities.name: Schopenhauer
entities.role: philosopher inspired by Kantianism

entities.name: Nietzsche
entities.role: philosopher inspired by Kantianism

entities.name: Fichte
entities.role: defender of German idealism

entities.name: Hegel
entities.role: defender of German idealism

entities.name: Engels

entities.name: Heidegger

entities.name: Gadamer
entities.role: 20th-century philosopher who pursued the tradition of German philosophy

entities.name: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
entities.role: catastrophic Roman defeat that led the Roman Empire to abandon plans to completely conquer Germany

entities.name: Battle of Königgrätz
entities.role: final battle of the German war in 1866, in which the Prussians defeated the Austrians

entities.name: Franco-Prussian War
entities.role: 1870 war in which Prussia and its southern German allies were victorious over France

entities.name: Thirty Years' War
entities.role: 1618–1648 conflict, one of the most destructive in European history, fought primarily in what is now Germany

entities.name: World War II
entities.role: conflict after which eastern European countries expelled Germans from their territories

entities.name: North German Confederation
entities.role: state created by Prussia's victory over Austria in 1866

entities.name: German Empire
entities.role: German nation-state created in 1871 that effectively excluded the multi-ethnic Austrian Habsburg monarchy and Liechtenstein

entities.name: German Confederation
entities.role: body within which German nationalism grew strongly before the 1866 war

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire
entities.role: empire in which Roman Catholicism was the sole established religion until the Reformation and where German was a lingua franca

entities.name: East Francia
entities.role: realm within which the kingdom of Germany formed, leading to German ethnicity in the Middle Ages

entities.name: Yiddish
entities.role: mixed language developed by Jews who assimilated into German culture, incorporating German and other European languages

entities.name: German language
entities.role: West Germanic native language of Germans, spoken by approximately 100 million native speakers

entities.name: Limes Germanicus
entities.role: frontier that was breached in AD 260

entities.name: Roman Catholic Church
entities.role: church Martin Luther challenged in 1517; Roman Catholics were 30.8% of Germany's population in the latest census

entities.name: Evangelical Church of Germany
entities.role: church whose membership is distinguished from other Protestant groups in the census figures

entities.name: New Apostolic Church
entities.role: Restorationist Christian church counted among 'others' in the census

entities.name: Hamburg
entities.role: German city with a non-religious majority

entities.name: Prussia
entities.role: kingdom that sought to unify Germany as Little Germany and fought Austria and France in the 19th century

entities.name: Austria
entities.role: country whose Habsburg monarchy was excluded from the German Empire and which fought Prussia in 1866
